tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

9	## Concept type
10	Academic capstone (TCC) built and evaluated with commercial-product customer-first discipline — no unit economics or customer-acquisition targets apply; the calibration used was feasibility, delivery-order fit, and scope-discipline-under-deadline-pressure instead.
11	
12	## Customer & problem (reconstructed — not stated anywhere in docs/input/)
13	- `docs/input/requirements.md` never names a customer or persona; it's organized entirely around RF01–RF10/screens. The persona below is a reconstruction from UI language (Portuguese), architectural choices, and explicit non-goals — flag this to any downstream PRD author as inferred, not sourced.
14	- Persona: a Brazilian Portuguese-speaking person who has already tried journaling (paper, Notes, Day One) and quit, or who uses a general-purpose chatbot (ChatGPT) to process their day and is frustrated it forgets everything between sessions.
15	- Problem: wants an AI that genuinely recalls and connects their own past entries (not generic "how did that make you feel" loops), without fear their private writing is mined, sold, or mistaken for a mental-health signal.
16	- Stakes: alternative today is journaling into a void that never responds, or using a memoryless, privacy-ambiguous general AI tool.
17	
18	## Core differentiator (validated against real 2025-2026 competitive research)
19	- "Generic AI response" fatigue is the #1 complaint across AI-journaling competitors (Reflectly, Day One AI, Mindsera) — Cerne's RAG-over-own-entries is positioned directly against this, not against feature count.
20	- Digital journal app market: $5.69B (2025) → $6.34B (2026), ~11.4% CAGR, projected $9.64B by 2030 — healthy, growing category; mobile is >60% of usage, validating the Flutter mobile-first bet.
21	- Real competitors with gaps worth knowing: Mindsera (feature-sprawl, gimmicky), Rosebud (therapist-designed framing risks implying clinical utility), Reflectly (mood-tracking-shallow, blurs into mental-health claims), Day One/Journey/Stoic (AI bolted on as paywalled add-on, not core).
22	- Regulatory climate rewards strict non-clinical positioning: Italy fined Replika's maker (Luka) €5M; California's 2026 law mandates companion-chatbot disclosure. Cerne's explicit non-clinical scope is a timing advantage, not just a constraint.
23	
24	## Honest, unresolved tension (the single most important thing for downstream PRD/architecture work to carry forward)
25	RF05, RF08, RF09 each explicitly scope grading to "mechanism only, never the quality of the generated narrative text" — meaning the dimension that actually determines whether a real user would stay (is the AI's insight good, or generic/canned) is never verified by this project's own acceptance criteria. This is a legitimate engineering-scope boundary, but it must be stated explicitly in any written defense/documentation — left implicit, it reads as an unexamined gap rather than a deliberate one.
26	
27	## Scope signals — in, out, and why
28	- IN (core, already specified): multimodal capture (RF01), STT/OCR (RF02), biometric vault (RF03), RAG chat (RF04), semantic search/filter (RF06), timeline history (RF07), save-chat-as-entry (RF10), proactive insight trigger mechanism only (RF08), AI summary export mechanism only (RF05), temporal dashboard (RF09).
29	- OUT (explicit extension features, never implement per AGENTS.md policy): dynamic AI categorization of entries (reduced to manual tags), autonomous AI goal extraction (reduced to static kanban with example cards), dynamic AI persona adjustment (reduced to a cosmetic settings toggle). These were deliberately cut for a solo/timeline-bound build, not because they lacked value — worth remembering if scope ever gets re-opened.
30	- OUT (hard non-goal, stated policy): any risk-signal detection (self-harm, suicidal ideation). Product is explicitly not framed as a mental-health app. No code path should ever imply otherwise.
31	- OUT (architectural constraint, not a product choice): per-entry edit/delete — entries are immutable; no `PATCH`/`DELETE /entries/:id` exists in the frozen backend. Real adoption-friction point for any future real-world use; cannot be changed within this project.
32	- OUT: offline writes — architecture is cloud-only; offline permits only viewing cached data, never creating entries.
33	
34	## Technical context / constraints for downstream architecture work
35	- Flutter/BLoC/Clean Architecture, iOS portrait-only, frozen Supabase backend (23 endpoints via `x-cerne-function` naming, never literal REST paths).
36	- AI split (server-side only, app never calls a provider directly): Claude Sonnet 5 for chat, Claude Haiku 4.5 for vision/OCR/PII-scrub/summaries/insights/dashboard narrative, Voyage AI voyage-4 for embeddings.
37	- Privacy/compliance baked into architecture: on-device Whisper STT (raw audio never leaves device — only the transcribed text syncs to the cloud), zero AI-pipeline data retention (RNF03), row-level security (RNF04), LGPD hard-delete (RNF05).
38	- RNF06: domain layer must import neither `package:flutter` nor anything from `data/`. RNF07: domain-layer test coverage ≥80%. RNF09: 5 write endpoints × 3 failure types = 15 tested network-failure scenarios.
39	- Delivery order (confirmed from requirements.md section 12): F000 → RF03 → RF01 → RF02 → RF07 → RF06 → RF04 → RF10 → RF08 → RF05 → RF09.
40	- **Unresolved contradiction, needs a decision before F000 implementation:** `_bmad-output/planning-artifacts/research/technical-flutter-package-selection-.../research.md` recommends `drift` (SQLite) for local cache; `_bmad-output/forge/f000-foundation-decisions/forged-idea.md` overrides it to `Hive`, reasoning all filtering/pagination is server-side so no relational engine is needed on-device. Fix: explicitly mark `drift` as superseded in the research artifact.
41	- Hardest unbuilt technical problems: RF07's history screen depends on three independently-changing streams (auth, sync-badge, entry data) while BLoCs may not import each other directly; RF08's proactive-insight trigger must fire exactly once per satisfied condition (5 messages OR 2 min inactivity) without double-firing or missing the window.
42	
43	## Resource & timeline (open, not estimated)
44	No deadline date, hours-per-week budget, or buffer exists anywhere in `docs/input/` or `_bmad-output/`. This is a genuine open question for the user (course calendar / defense date), not something inferable from the input package. Feasibility of the delivery order against RNF07/RNF09's testing bars cannot be assessed until this is known.
45	
46	## Rejected framings (press release stage)
47	- Headline candidate "Cerne Lets You Actually Talk to Your Own Diary — Privately, and It Remembers" — rejected as too long, stacking unproven claims ("actually," "privately") directly in the headline.
48	- Any "AI companion" / "AI friend" framing — rejected deliberately, to stay clear of the companion-chatbot category currently under regulatory/reputational pressure (Replika-class fines and lawsuits).
49	- Leading with the on-device-privacy angle instead of the memory angle — rejected as the headline hook because "AI forgets me / generic responses" tested as the louder, more universal pain point in research; privacy is used as a supporting proof point instead.
50	
51	## Known gaps flagged during Customer/Internal FAQ (actionable items)
52	- **Fast-follow, low cost:** add a static crisis-resources disclaimer/link — requires no detection logic, doesn't contradict the non-clinical scope, closes an uncomfortable silent gap (no mental-health signposting at all today).
53	- **Accepted trade-off, not fixable within this project:** per-entry immutability (no edit/delete); cloud-only writes (no offline capture); no automatic entry categorization.
54	- **Process fix, cheap:** reconcile the drift-vs-Hive contradiction before F000 starts.
55	- **Documentation fix, not a code change:** the written defense must explicitly name the mechanism-vs-quality scope boundary (see "Honest, unresolved tension" above) rather than leaving it implicit.
56	- **Undecided, needs the user's explicit call:** whether Cerne is a one-time academic artifact or is meant to survive into a job-application portfolio — changes how much distribution/"Getting Started" planning matters going forward.
57	
58	## Verdict summary
59	Forged in steel: the memory/RAG differentiator (research-validated against real competitor gaps), the precisely-qualified privacy architecture, the non-clinical positioning as a timing advantage, and the already-demonstrated resource discipline (three extension features concretely cut, on record). Needs more heat: timeline/deadline (completely unknown), post-defense fate of the project, two cheap unactioned fixes (drift/Hive, crisis disclaimer). Cracks in the foundation: the quality-of-AI-insight scope boundary must be stated explicitly in the defense or it reads as an unexamined gap rather than a deliberate one; entry immutability is a real adoption-friction point that should be named as a known limitation rather than silently discovered later.

- **Accepted trade-off, not fixable within this project:** per-entry immutability (no edit/delete); cloud-only writes (no offline capture); no automatic entry categorization.
- **Process fix, cheap:** reconcile the drift-vs-Hive contradiction before F000 starts.
- **Documentation fix, not a code change:** the written defense must explicitly name the mechanism-vs-quality scope boundary (see "Honest, unresolved tension" above) rather than leaving it implicit.
- **Undecided, needs the user's explicit call:** whether Cerne is a one-time academic artifact or is meant to survive into a job-application portfolio — changes how much distribution/"Getting Started" planning matters going forward.

## Verdict summary
Forged in steel: the memory/RAG differentiator (research-validated against real competitor gaps), the precisely-qualified privacy architecture, the non-clinical positioning as a timing advantage, and the already-demonstrated resource discipline (three extension features concretely cut, on record). Needs more heat: timeline/deadline (completely unknown), post-defense fate of the project, two cheap unactioned fixes (drift/Hive, crisis disclaimer). 9	- **DI: plain get_it.** No injectable/codegen. Per-feature registration function, called from main.
10	- **DTOs/entities: freezed + json_serializable.** Justified by field count, not blanket codegen — Entry has 11 required fields in the contract; hand-written `==`/`copyWith` for that is a bug magnet. Also used for sealed unions (Failure, Resource).

# Product Brief Template

A flexible starting structure for the executive product brief. Adapt aggressively to the product, the purpose, and the domain. Drop sections that do not earn their place, add sections the product needs, reorder freely. The brief serves the product's story, not the template's shape.

## Default Structure

```markdown
# Product Brief: {Product Name}

## Executive Summary

[2-3 paragraph narrative: what this is, what problem it solves, why it matters, why now. Compelling enough to stand alone — if someone reads only this section, they should understand the vision.]

## The Problem

[What pain exists, who feels it, how they cope today, the cost of the status quo. Be specific: real scenarios, real frustrations, real consequences.]

## The Solution

[What is being built, how it solves the problem. Focus on the experience and the outcome, not the implementation.]

## What Makes This Different

[Key differentiators. Why this approach over alternatives, what is the unfair advantage. Be honest. If the moat is execution speed, say so. Do not fabricate technical moats.]

## Who This Serves

[Primary users — vivid but brief. Who they are, what they need, what success looks like for them. Secondary users if relevant.]

## Success Criteria

[How we know this is working. Mix of user success signals and business objectives. Measurable.]

## Scope

[What is in for the first version. What is explicitly out. Keep this tight — boundary document, not a feature list.]

## Vision

[Where this goes if it succeeds. What it becomes in 2-3 years. Inspiring but grounded.]
```
---
# DO NOT EDIT -- overwritten on every update.
#
# Workflow customization surface for bmad-product-brief.
#
# Override files (not edited here):
#   {project-root}/_bmad/custom/bmad-product-brief.toml         (team)
#   {project-root}/_bmad/custom/bmad-product-brief.user.toml    (personal)

[workflow]

# --- Configurable below. Overrides merge per BMad structural rules: ---
#   scalars: override wins • arrays: append

# Steps to run before the standard activation (config load, greet).
# Use for pre-flight loads, compliance checks, etc.
activation_steps_prepend = []

# Steps to run after greet but before the workflow begins.
# Use for context-heavy setup that should happen once the user has been acknowledged.
activation_steps_append = []

# Persistent facts the workflow keeps in mind for the whole run
# (standards, compliance constraints, stylistic guardrails).
# Each entry is either a literal sentence, a skill prefixed with `skill:`, or a `file:`-prefixed path/glob
# whose contents are loaded as facts.
#
# Default loads project-context.md if bmad-generate-project-context has produced one — this gives
# the facilitator persistent awareness of the project's tech, domain, and constraints without
# re-asking. Common opt-ins (set in team/user override TOML):
#   "skill:acme-co:terms-and-conditions"                                      # a skill that contains some relevant info
#   "Elvis has left the building"                                             # generic agent instruction
persistent_facts = [
  "file:{project-root}/**/project-context.md",
]

# Executed when the workflow completes (after the user has been told the
# brief is ready). Accepts either a string scalar (single instruction)
# or an array of instructions executed in order. Empty for none.
on_complete = ""

# Default brief structure. Treated as a starting point — the LLM adapts it
# to the product, purpose, and domain. Override the path in team/user TOML
# to enforce a different structure (e.g. regulated-industry, investor-deck).
brief_template = "assets/brief-template.md"

# Run folder location. The brief and optional addendum land inside `{brief_output_path}/{run_folder_pattern}/`.
# Resume-check scans `{brief_output_path}` for prior unfinished runs.
brief_output_path = "{planning_artifacts}/briefs"
run_folder_pattern = "brief-{project_name}-{date}"

# Document standards applied to human-consumed docs at finalize. Each entry is
# a `skill:`, `file:`, or plain-text directive; the parent LLM applies the
# findings before the user sees the draft. Encodes standards, not options.
#
# Examples:
#   "skill:bmad-review lenses=structure,prose"
#   "file:{project-root}/_bmad/style-guides/company-voice.md"
#   "Convert all dates to ISO 8601 format."
#
# Suggested order (broader passes first, narrower last):
#   1. Structural (cuts, reorganization, section sizing)
#   2. Content/voice/conventions (org standards, tone, terminology, compliance)
#   3. Prose mechanics (grammar, clarity, typos)
#
# Override the array in team/user TOML to add additional standards. Append-only:
# base entries cannot be removed or replaced (resolver has no removal mechanism).
# The default entry runs bmad-review's two editorial lenses in order:
# structure, then prose on top of the structure findings. The `lenses=` suffix
# names them; drop it to let bmad-review pick what fits the content.
doc_standards = [
  "skill:bmad-review lenses=structure,prose",
]

# External-source registry. Natural-language directives describing knowledge
# bases, MCP tools, or internal systems the LLM may consult during the workflow
# when a relevant need surfaces. The LLM does NOT query these preemptively —
# it consults them on demand (during Discovery, validation, drafting, etc.).
# Each entry names the tool, the conditions for using it, and any fields the
# tool needs. If a named MCP tool is unavailable at runtime, the LLM falls
# back to standard behavior and notes the gap. Empty by default.
#
# Examples (set in team/user override TOML):
#   "When researching internal product context, consult corp:kb_search (database='product-docs') before web search."
#   "For voice-of-customer signal during Discovery, query corp:feedback_search with project={project_name}."
#   "When validating domain-compliance claims for a healthcare brief, cross-check against corp:hipaa_reference."
external_sources = []

# External-handoff routing. Natural-language directives the LLM applies at
# Finalize to route outputs beyond local files (Confluence, Notion, Google
# Drive, ticket systems, etc.). Each entry names the MCP tool, the destination,
# and the fields the tool needs. Handoffs run after the artifact is polished
# and before the final user-facing message. URLs or IDs returned by the
# destination are captured and surfaced to the user. If a named tool is
# unavailable at runtime, the handoff is skipped and flagged in the JSON
# status; local files always exist regardless. Fires automatically — users
# can opt out in their prompt for a specific run. Empty by default.
#
# Examples (set in team/user override TOML):
#   "After finalize, upload brief.md and addendum.md to Confluence via corp:confluence_upload (space_key='PROD', parent_page='Product Briefs', label='brief', author={user_name})."
#   "Post a ready-for-review ping to Slack via corp:slack_post (channel='#product', text='New brief: '+{confluence_url})."
external_handoffs = []

1	# Cerne — Requirements and Screen Flow
2	
3	Cerne is a reflective-journaling mobile app with an AI assistant. The user records their day by text, audio or photo; a conversational agent consults those records (semantic search) to answer with context and to offer insights.
4	
5	This document is the product specification. The visual reference is the prototype in `docs/input/prototype/`; the backend API is documented in `docs/input/backend/`.
6	
7	---
8	
9	## 1. Functional requirements
10	
11	### RF01 — Multimodal capture (text / audio / photo)
12	Data entry by text, real-time audio recording and photo upload — always through Screen 2 (Insertion Modal), which has a raw text field in addition to the microphone and the gallery. Every capture becomes a persisted record (`POST /entries`), **distinct from a chat message** (see the separation note in RF04).
13	
14	**Acceptance criteria:**
15	- The three modalities (text, audio, photo) result in the same persisted-entry format — none is treated structurally differently from the others after capture.
16	- Cancelling a capture midway (e.g., interrupting a recording) does not create a partial or empty entry.
17	
18	### RF02 — Speech-to-text / OCR processing
19	Transcription of audio (speech-to-text) and recognition of text in images (OCR) over the content captured in RF01.
20	
21	**Acceptance criteria:** four visible states — recording, processing, transcribed, transcription error.
22	
23	### RF03 — Biometric authentication vault
24	Access barrier via Face ID / Touch ID / PIN before exposing the user's data.
25	
26	**Acceptance criteria:**
27	- A biometric failure (e.g., fingerprint not recognized) offers PIN as an alternative, without locking the user out of the app.
28	- The app, sent to the background and resumed after 5 minutes, requires authentication again — it does not stay unlocked indefinitely (fixed value, not configurable by the user).
29	
30	### RF04 — Interactive chat with memory (RAG)
31	Continuous conversation with the AI agent, with semantic search over previous entries. **Chat messages are conversational and do not create journal entries automatically** — the only exception is the explicit save action described in RF10. Otherwise, the chat queries existing entries via RAG but does not write to them.
32	
33	**Acceptance criteria:**
34	- Three mandatory UI states: processing/streaming, error, complete response.
35	- If the response stream drops midway, the partial message stays visible with a failure indication (it does not disappear).
36	
37	### RF05 — Personal summary export
38	Generation of a narrative summary by AI (Claude Haiku 4.5) from the user's entries, exportable as PDF, with an additional option to download the raw data without the narrative. No clinical or diagnostic connotation. **Scope: job generation, file download and failure handling — never the quality of the generated narrative text.**
39	
40	**Acceptance criteria:**
41	- An export job with zero entries in the period returns a handled error state (not an empty PDF, not a crash).
42	- A failure generating the narrative text (model timeout) still allows downloading the raw data without the narrative — the export is not blocked by an AI failure.
43	
44	### RF06 — Semantic search / filter over journal entries
45	Semantic similarity search (via Voyage AI embeddings, reusing the ones already generated in RF01) combined with metadata filters (date, entry type). There is no filter by tag or category: the backend does not implement it in any endpoint — `GET /entries` and `GET /entries/search` accept only `source` and `dateFrom`/`dateTo`. Tags appear only embedded, read-only, in the `Entry` object (see section 2).
46	
47	**Acceptance criteria:**
48	- Searching for a term finds semantically related entries even without the exact word (e.g., searching "ansiedade" returns an entry that only mentions "nervosismo", without the literal term).
49	- 300 ms search debounce: fast typing triggers a single query, not one per keystroke.
50	- Results from the local read cache stay consistent with the server after reconnection, without duplicating displayed items *(the architecture is cloud-only; offline allows only viewing already-cached data, not writing)*.
51	- Two or more filters applied at the same time (`source` + `dateFrom`/`dateTo`) narrow results with AND logic (not OR).
52	- Clearing the filters returns to the full list without restarting the screen.
53	
54	### RF07 — Multi-source history (timeline)
55	A screen whose state depends simultaneously on authentication, synchronization status and entry data.
56	
57	**Acceptance criteria:**
58	- Session expiration while viewing triggers a new-login prompt without a crash and without losing the scroll position.
59	- The per-entry synchronization status badge updates independently of the authentication stream.
60	- No BLoC imports another BLoC directly.
61	
62	### RF08 — Proactive insights (mechanism)
63	A suggestion inserted into the chat without the user asking for it. **Scope: only the trigger mechanism, never the quality of the generated text.**
64	
65	**Acceptance criteria:**
66	- Trigger after N = 5 user messages OR T = 2 min of inactivity — fires exactly once per satisfied condition.
67	- If insight generation fails (timeout / network error), the main chat keeps working normally.
68	- Dismissing the insight does not change the scroll position or the state of the main conversation.
69	
70	### RF09 — Temporal summaries / dashboard
71	An evolution chart with a textual summary, computed on demand when the Settings tab is opened. **Scope: aggregation and rendering, never the quality of the narrative text.**
72	
73	**Acceptance criteria:**
74	- Renders correctly in three scenarios: zero entries, one entry, more than 30 entries.
75	- The aggregation recalculates correctly after an entry is created (cache-invalidation test). Entries are immutable: there is no `PATCH /entries/:id` or `DELETE /entries/:id` in the backend, and no screen describes an edit or delete action on an entry.
76	- The AI narrative text is checked only for not breaking the UI in extreme cases — never for its content.
77	
78	### RF10 — Save a chat message as an entry
79	A button on each user message in the chat that converts it into a persisted entry — for moments when the user states relevant information during the conversation, not only through dedicated capture (RF01). It reuses the same `POST /entries` pipeline (PII check + embedding), with the origin marked as `chat`.
80	
81	**Acceptance criteria:**
82	- The chat feature triggers the creation of the entry through a shared interface / use case, never by directly importing a repository or data source of the entries feature — a violation here also breaks RNF06.
83	- Saving the same message twice does not create duplicate entries (idempotency).
84	- A failure to save (network unavailable) keeps the conversation working normally, and the button returns to a state that allows trying again — the same failure-isolation pattern as RF08.
85	- Only user messages have the button — AI responses cannot become entries.
86	
87	---
88	
89	## 2. Extension features — not implemented
90	
91	They keep the "essence" of the original product flow and exist in the prototype, but **receive no functional implementation**. A menu entry may exist as a placeholder.
92	
93	| Original feature | Treatment in the current version |
94	|---|---|
95	| Dynamic categorization (AI) | Simplified to manual tags created by the user (My Records screen) |
96	| Autonomous goal extraction | Action Plans screen — static, no logic |
97	| Dynamic persona adjustment | Simple cosmetic toggle (Settings), low cost to maintain |
98	
99	---
100	
101	## 3. Quality requirements
102	
103	| ID | Requirement | Target |
104	|---|---|---|
105	| RNF06 | Zero layer violations — the domain layer does not import `package:flutter` nor classes from `data/` | 0 violations |
106	| RNF07 | Minimum test coverage of the domain layer (`lib/**/domain/**`) | ≥ 80% |
107	| RNF08 | Visual fidelity to the prototype — the primary color matches the prototype's hex value, typography matches family and size, spacing matches the prototype; no visual value hardcoded outside the central file `design_tokens.dart` | Every screen faithful in color, typography and spacing; 0 hardcoded values |
108	| RNF09 | Consistent network-error handling — `Either<Failure, T>` pattern via `fpdart` in every repository; every write endpoint (5 endpoints) handles three failure types — timeout, malformed response, no connection — covered by tests with `mocktail` | 0 repository signatures outside the pattern; 15 of 15 scenarios handled |
109	
110	## 4. Other non-functional requirements
111	
112	RNF01 — Interaction latency (a local action is reflected in the UI in < 100 ms; any network call above 300 ms shows a loading indicator) · RNF02 — PII stripping (via Claude Haiku 4.5 with a structured prompt / tool use, not a dedicated NER model) · RNF03 — Zero data retention · RNF04 — RLS (Row Level Security) · RNF05 — Hard delete of account and data (LGPD).
113	
114	**Known limitation:** the system has no protocol for detecting or responding to risk signals (suicidal ideation, self-harm) in entries or chat messages. Since the product is not framed as a mental-health app, this absence is an explicit scope decision.
115	
116	---
117	
118	## 5. Interface architecture and screen flow
119	
120	### 5.1 Visual foundation (design system)
121	Minimalist identity, a warm and neutral palette, readable sans-serif typography, standardized components (buttons, chat bubbles, cards). This foundation is the direct object of RNF08. Tokens: `docs/input/prototype/prototype-extract.md`.
122	
123	### 5.2 Screens
124	
125	**Screen 0 — Splash:** initial loading; checks the connection and syncs the cache in the background. *Connects to: RF06, RNF01.*
126	
127	**Screen 0.1 — Authentication vault:** biometric/PIN barrier before access. *Connects to: RF03.*
128	
129	**Screen 1 — Home (chat):** main screen, continuous conversation, "+" button for multimodal input, AI status indicator, "save to journal" button on each user message. *Connects to: RF04, RF08, RF10, RNF01, RNF09.*
130	
131	**Screen 2 — Insertion Modal:** overlay with three ways to capture — raw text field, microphone (audio) and gallery/camera (photo) — with a transcription indicator. Every capture here creates a persisted entry, never a chat message. *Connects to: RF01, RF02.*
132	
133	**Screen 3 — Side menu (sidebar):** navigation hub, session history, access to My Records / Action Plans / Settings, and a "Novo Chat" button that opens Screen 1 in its empty state. *Connects to: RF04 (via the "Novo Chat" button); the other items are pure navigation.*
134	
135	**Screen 4 — My Records:** consolidated timeline, filters, manual tags (extension, section 2), export. *Connects to: RF07, RF06, RF05.*
136	
137	**Screen 5 — Action Plans:** simple Kanban board (columns "A Fazer" / "Em Andamento" / "Concluído") with static example cards. *(Extension — section 2.)*
138	
139	**Screen 6 — Settings and profile:** evolution dashboard, persona selector — "Analítico" / "Empático" / "Socrático" (extension, section 2; it would only change the system-prompt string of RF04), delete account. *Connects to: RF09, RNF05.*
140	
141	---
142	
143	## 6. Backend endpoint inventory
144	
145	The backend is already built and frozen. The API contract, `docs/input/backend/api/openapi.yaml`, is the source of truth; this section is a reading of it oriented by screen and requirement. How to build the real URL of each operation: `docs/input/backend/README.md`.
146	
147	Every endpoint returns errors in the standard contract of RNF09 — `{ code, message, retryable }` — and is protected by RLS in Supabase. AI providers: Claude (chat, vision/OCR, summary, insights, dashboard, PII detection) and Voyage AI (embeddings) — the backend's only two external AI dependencies. Audio transcription (speech-to-text) runs on-device (Whisper) and never reaches the backend as an audio file.
148	
149	### 6.1 Authentication and session
150	| Endpoint | Requirement | AI involved |
151	|---|---|---|
152	| `POST /auth/signup` | RF03 | — |
153	| `POST /auth/login` | RF03 | — |
154	| `POST /auth/refresh` | RF03, RF07 | — |
155	| `GET /auth/session` | RF07 | — |
156	| `POST /auth/logout` | RF03 | — |
157	
158	**No "biometric-unlock" endpoint — intentional:** the Face ID / Touch ID / PIN barrier of Screen 0.1 is validated entirely on the device, never on the server. The backend only stores the preference (`biometricEnabled`, read and written via `PATCH /account/settings`, section 6.7) — it validates no biometrics. After passing the local barrier, the app uses the existing session (renewed via `POST /auth/refresh` when needed, or `POST /auth/login` if it has fully expired).
159	
160	### 6.2 Ingestion and entries
161	| Endpoint | Requirement | AI involved |
162	|---|---|---|
163	| `POST /media/ocr` — the image is not persisted; only the extracted text moves on | RF02 | Claude Haiku 4.5 (vision) |
164	| `POST /entries` — creates an entry; internally triggers the PII check and embedding generation; accepts `source` (`manual`/`audio`/`photo`/`chat`) and `chatMessageId` when the origin is the chat | RF01, RF02, RF10 | Claude Haiku 4.5 (PII) + Voyage AI (embedding) |
165	| `GET /entries` — filters by `source`/`dateFrom`/`dateTo`; tags appear only embedded in the response, read-only | RF07 | — |
166	| `GET /entries/:id` | RF07 | — |
167	
168	**No entry editing or deletion, and no tag endpoint — intentional:** entries are immutable once created ("original content intact, never censored"); there is no `PATCH`/`DELETE /entries/:id`. Tags are populated only by test seed data — no endpoint creates, deletes or filters by tag or category (see RF06). This is consistent with section 2: dynamic categorization was simplified to manual tags that receive no functional implementation.
169	
170	### 6.3 Chat and memory (RAG)
171	| Endpoint | Requirement | AI involved |
172	|---|---|---|
173	| `POST /chat/sessions` — blocked offline | RF04 | — |
174	| `GET /chat/sessions` — works offline (cache) | RF04, RF07 | — |
175	| `GET /chat/sessions/:id/messages` — works offline (cache) | RF04 | — |
176	| `POST /chat/sessions/:id/messages` — streaming (SSE); blocked offline | RF04 | Voyage AI (question embedding) + Claude Sonnet 5 (response) |
177	| `POST /chat/sessions/:id/messages/:userMessageId/retry` — regenerates the response without duplicating the user's question; it supports "partial message visible with a failure indication, and a way to try again" in RF04 | RF04 | Voyage AI (embedding, reused from cache) + Claude Sonnet 5 (response) |
178	| `POST /chat/sessions/:id/insight` | RF08 | Claude Haiku 4.5 |
179	| `POST /entries` — called from the "save to journal" button (see 6.2) | RF10 | Claude Haiku 4.5 (PII) + Voyage AI (embedding) |
180	
181	### 6.4 Search
182	| Endpoint | Requirement | AI involved |
183	|---|---|---|
184	| `GET /entries/search?q=&source=&dateFrom=&dateTo=&limit=` — no `category` (see RF06) | RF06 | Voyage AI (query embedding) |
185	
186	### 6.5 Export
187	| Endpoint | Requirement | AI involved |
188	|---|---|---|
189	| `POST /export/summary` — asynchronous job | RF05 | Claude Haiku 4.5 |
190	| `GET /export/:jobId/status` | RF05 | — |
191	| `GET /export/:jobId/download` | RF05 | — |
192	
193	### 6.6 Dashboard
194	| Endpoint | Requirement | AI involved |
195	|---|---|---|
196	| `GET /dashboard/aggregate?period=` — separate from the text so it does not block the chart | RF09 | — |
197	| `GET /dashboard/narrative?period=` | RF09 | Claude Haiku 4.5 |
198	
199	### 6.7 Account
200	| Endpoint | Requirement | AI involved |
201	|---|---|---|
202	| `PATCH /account/settings` — includes the persona toggle (extension) | RNF05, extension | — |
203	| `DELETE /account` | RNF05 | — |
204

206

320	| Parameter | Value | Requirement |
321	|---|---|---|

323	| Search debounce | 300 ms | RF06 |
324	| Proactive insight trigger | 5 messages OR 2 min of inactivity | RF08 |
325	| Dashboard rendering scenarios | 0 / 1 / > 30 entries | RF09 |
326	| Minimum test coverage (domain) | ≥ 80% | RNF07 |
327	| Local UI latency | < 100 ms | RNF01 |
328	| Loading-indicator threshold | > 300 ms | RNF01 |

333	## 11. Error codes (RNF09)
334	
335	Every endpoint returns `{ code, message, retryable }`. Minimum codes the app handles:
336	
337	| Code | Situation | `retryable` |
338	|---|---|---|
339	| `AUTH_EXPIRED` | Session expired, re-authentication needed | no |
340	| `AUTH_INVALID` | Invalid credentials / biometrics | no |
341	| `NETWORK_TIMEOUT` | Request exceeded the time limit | yes |
342	| `NETWORK_OFFLINE` | No connection — action blocked (see RF04/RF06) | yes |
343	| `VALIDATION_ERROR` | Malformed request body | no |
344	| `PII_CHECK_FAILED` | PII check failed before persisting | yes |
345	| `EMBEDDING_FAILED` | Voyage AI unavailable / error | yes |
346	| `AI_GENERATION_TIMEOUT` | Claude did not respond in time (chat/insight/summary/dashboard) | yes |
347	| `NOT_FOUND` | Resource does not exist or does not belong to the user | no |
348	| `RATE_LIMITED` | Request limit exceeded | yes |
349	
350	The complete, closed list of the backend's 13 codes, with HTTP statuses, is in `docs/input/backend/error-taxonomy.md`.
351	
352	---
353	
354	## 12. Delivery order
355	
356	Work is delivered in units, one per functional requirement, preceded by a foundation unit, in this order:
357	
358	**F000 → RF03 → RF01 → RF02 → RF07 → RF06 → RF04 → RF10 → RF08 → RF05 → RF09**
359	
360	- **F000 (foundation)** covers what no single requirement owns but all of them use: project scaffold, `design_tokens.dart`, HTTP client returning `Either`, login and sign-up (Screen 0.1a in the prototype), base navigation and expired-session handling.
361	- RF10 comes after RF01 and RF04; RF08 comes after RF04.
362	
363	---
364	
365	## 13. Technical constraints
366	
367	**Fixed:**
368	- Flutter and Dart at the version pinned for the repository (fvm).
369	- State management: `flutter_bloc`.
370	- Clean Architecture, three layers per feature.
371	- Error handling: `fpdart`; repositories return `Either<Failure, T>`.
372	- Test doubles: `mocktail`.
373	- On-device speech-to-text: `whisper_ggml`.
374	- Visual tokens: `lib/core/design_tokens.dart` is the single source of colors, typography, spacing and radii.
375	- Platform: iOS, portrait only.
376	- Folder convention:
377	
378	```
379	lib/
380	  core/
381	  features/
382	    <feature>/
383	      data/
384	      domain/
385	      presentation/
386	```
387	
388	**Free (choose what fits):** routing, HTTP client, local cache, dependency injection, secure storage, biometrics package, chart package.

# Cerne — Requirements and Screen Flow

Cerne is a reflective-journaling mobile app with an AI assistant. The user records their day by text, audio or photo; a conversational agent consults those records (semantic search) to answer with context and to offer insights.

This document is the product specification. The visual reference is the prototype in `docs/input/prototype/`; the backend API is documented in `docs/input/backend/`.

---

## 1. Functional requirements

### RF01 — Multimodal capture (text / audio / photo)
Data entry by text, real-time audio recording and photo upload — always through Screen 2 (Insertion Modal), which has a raw text field in addition to the microphone and the gallery. Every capture becomes a persisted record (`POST /entries`), **distinct from a chat message** (see the separation note in RF04).

**Acceptance criteria:**
- The three modalities (text, audio, photo) result in the same persisted-entry format — none is treated structurally differently from the others after capture.
- Cancelling a capture midway (e.g., interrupting a recording) does not create a partial or empty entry.

### RF02 — Speech-to-text / OCR processing
Transcription of audio (speech-to-text) and recognition of text in images (OCR) over the content captured in RF01.

**Acceptance criteria:** four visible states — recording, processing, transcribed, transcription error.

### RF03 — Biometric authentication vault
Access barrier via Face ID / Touch ID / PIN before exposing the user's data.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- A biometric failure (e.g., fingerprint not recognized) offers PIN as an alternative, without locking the user out of the app.
- The app, sent to the background and resumed after 5 minutes, requires authentication again — it does not stay unlocked indefinitely (fixed value, not configurable by the user).

### RF04 — Interactive chat with memory (RAG)
Continuous conversation with the AI agent, with semantic search over previous entries. **Chat messages are conversational and do not create journal entries automatically** — the only exception is the explicit save action described in RF10. Otherwise, the chat queries existing entries via RAG but does not write to them.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- Three mandatory UI states: processing/streaming, error, complete response.
- If the response stream drops midway, the partial message stays visible with a failure indication (it does not disappear).

### RF05 — Personal summary export
Generation of a narrative summary by AI (Claude Haiku 4.5) from the user's entries, exportable as PDF, with an additional option to download the raw data without the narrative. No clinical or diagnostic connotation. **Scope: job generation, file download and failure handling — never the quality of the generated narrative text.**

**Acceptance criteria:**
- An export job with zero entries in the period returns a handled error state (not an empty PDF, not a crash).
- A failure generating the narrative text (model timeout) still allows downloading the raw data without the narrative — the export is not blocked by an AI failure.

### RF06 — Semantic search / filter over journal entries
Semantic similarity search (via Voyage AI embeddings, reusing the ones already generated in RF01) combined with metadata filters (date, entry type). There is no filter by tag or category: the backend does not implement it in any endpoint — `GET /entries` and `GET /entries/search` accept only `source` and `dateFrom`/`dateTo`. Tags appear only embedded, read-only, in the `Entry` object (see section 2).

**Acceptance criteria:**
- Searching for a term finds semantically related entries even without the exact word (e.g., searching "ansiedade" returns an entry that only mentions "nervosismo", without the literal term).
- 300 ms search debounce: fast typing triggers a single query, not one per keystroke.
- Results from the local read cache stay consistent with the server after reconnection, without duplicating displayed items *(the architecture is cloud-only; offline allows only viewing already-cached data, not writing)*.
- Two or more filters applied at the same time (`source` + `dateFrom`/`dateTo`) narrow results with AND logic (not OR).
- Clearing the filters returns to the full list without restarting the screen.

### RF07 — Multi-source history (timeline)
A screen whose state depends simultaneously on authentication, synchronization status and entry data.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- Session expiration while viewing triggers a new-login prompt without a crash and without losing the scroll position.
- The per-entry synchronization status badge updates independently of the authentication stream.
- No BLoC imports another BLoC directly.

### RF08 — Proactive insights (mechanism)
A suggestion inserted into the chat without the user asking for it. **Scope: only the trigger mechanism, never the quality of the generated text.**

**Acceptance criteria:**
- Trigger after N = 5 user messages OR T = 2 min of inactivity — fires exactly once per satisfied condition.
- If insight generation fails (timeout / network error), the main chat keeps working normally.
- Dismissing the insight does not change the scroll position or the state of the main conversation.

### RF09 — Temporal summaries / dashboard
An evolution chart with a textual summary, computed on demand when the Settings tab is opened. **Scope: aggregation and rendering, never the quality of the narrative text.**

**Acceptance criteria:**
- Renders correctly in three scenarios: zero entries, one entry, more than 30 entries.
- The aggregation recalculates correctly after an entry is created (cache-invalidation test). Entries are immutable: there is no `PATCH /entries/:id` or `DELETE /entries/:id` in the backend, and no screen describes an edit or delete action on an entry.
- The AI narrative text is checked only for not breaking the UI in extreme cases — never for its content.

### RF10 — Save a chat message as an entry
A button on each user message in the chat that converts it into a persisted entry — for moments when the user states relevant information during the conversation, not only through dedicated capture (RF01). It reuses the same `POST /entries` pipeline (PII check + embedding), with the origin marked as `chat`.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- The chat feature triggers the creation of the entry through a shared interface / use case, never by directly importing a repository or data source of the entries feature — a violation here also breaks RNF06.
- Saving the same message twice does not create duplicate entries (idempotency).
- A failure to save (network unavailable) keeps the conversation working normally, and the button returns to a state that allows trying again — the same failure-isolation pattern as RF08.
- Only user messages have the button — AI responses cannot become entries.

---

## 2. Extension features — not implemented

They keep the "essence" of the original product flow and exist in the prototype, but **receive no functional implementation**. A menu entry may exist as a placeholder.

| Original feature | Treatment in the current version |
|---|---|
| Dynamic categorization (AI) | Simplified to manual tags created by the user (My Records screen) |
| Autonomous goal extraction | Action Plans screen — static, no logic |
| Dynamic persona adjustment | Simple cosmetic toggle (Settings), low cost to maintain |

---

## 3. Quality requirements

| ID | Requirement | Target |
|---|---|---|
| RNF06 | Zero layer violations — the domain layer does not import `package:flutter` nor classes from `data/` | 0 violations |
| RNF07 | Minimum test coverage of the domain layer (`lib/**/domain/**`) | ≥ 80% |
| RNF08 | Visual fidelity to the prototype — the primary color matches the prototype's hex value, typography matches family and size, spacing matches the prototype; no visual value hardcoded outside the central file `design_tokens.dart` | Every screen faithful in color, typography and spacing; 0 hardcoded values |
| RNF09 | Consistent network-error handling — `Either<Failure, T>` pattern via `fpdart` in every repository; every write endpoint (5 endpoints) handles three failure types — timeout, malformed response, no connection — covered by tests with `mocktail` | 0 repository signatures outside the pattern; 15 of 15 scenarios handled |

## 4. Other non-functional requirements

RNF01 — Interaction latency (a local action is reflected in the UI in < 100 ms; any network call above 300 ms shows a loading indicator) · RNF02 — PII stripping (via Claude Haiku 4.5 with a structured prompt / tool use, not a dedicated NER model) · RNF03 — Zero data retention · RNF04 — RLS (Row Level Security) · RNF05 — Hard delete of account and data (LGPD).

**Known limitation:** the system has no protocol for detecting or responding to risk signals (suicidal ideation, self-harm) in entries or chat messages. Since the product is not framed as a mental-health app, this absence is an explicit scope decision.

---

## 5. Interface architecture and screen flow

### 5.1 Visual foundation (design system)
Minimalist identity, a warm and neutral palette, readable sans-serif typography, standardized components (buttons, chat bubbles, cards). This foundation is the direct object of RNF08. Tokens: `docs/input/prototype/prototype-extract.md`.

### 5.2 Screens

**Screen 0 — Splash:** initial loading; checks the connection and syncs the cache in the background. *Connects to: RF06, RNF01.*

**Screen 0.1 — Authentication vault:** biometric/PIN barrier before access. *Connects to: RF03.*

**Screen 1 — Home (chat):** main screen, continuous conversation, "+" button for multimodal input, AI status indicator, "save to journal" button on each user message. *Connects to: RF04, RF08, RF10, RNF01, RNF09.*

**Screen 2 — Insertion Modal:** overlay with three ways to capture — raw text field, microphone (audio) and gallery/camera (photo) — with a transcription indicator. Every capture here creates a persisted entry, never a chat message. *Connects to: RF01, RF02.*

**Screen 3 — Side menu (sidebar):** navigation hub, session history, access to My Records / Action Plans / Settings, and a "Novo Chat" button that opens Screen 1 in its empty state. *Connects to: RF04 (via the "Novo Chat" button); the other items are pure navigation.*

**Screen 4 — My Records:** consolidated timeline, filters, manual tags (extension, section 2), export. *Connects to: RF07, RF06, RF05.*

**Screen 5 — Action Plans:** simple Kanban board (columns "A Fazer" / "Em Andamento" / "Concluído") with static example cards. *(Extension — section 2.)*

**Screen 6 — Settings and profile:** evolution dashboard, persona selector — "Analítico" / "Empático" / "Socrático" (extension, section 2; it would only change the system-prompt string of RF04), delete account. *Connects to: RF09, RNF05.*

---

## 6. Backend endpoint inventory

The backend is already built and frozen. The API contract, `docs/input/backend/api/openapi.yaml`, is the source of truth; this section is a reading of it oriented by screen and requirement. How to build the real URL of each operation: `docs/input/backend/README.md`.

Every endpoint returns errors in the standard contract of RNF09 — `{ code, message, retryable }` — and is protected by RLS in Supabase. AI providers: Claude (chat, vision/OCR, summary, insights, dashboard, PII detection) and Voyage AI (embeddings) — the backend's only two external AI dependencies. Audio transcription (speech-to-text) runs on-device (Whisper) and never reaches the backend as an audio file.

### 6.1 Authentication and session
| Endpoint | Requirement | AI involved |
|---|---|---|
| `POST /auth/signup` | RF03 | — |
| `POST /auth/login` | RF03 | — |
| `POST /auth/refresh` | RF03, RF07 | — |
| `GET /auth/session` | RF07 | — |
| `POST /auth/logout` | RF03 | — |

**No "biometric-unlock" endpoint — intentional:** the Face ID / Touch ID / PIN barrier of Screen 0.1 is validated entirely on the device, never on the server. The backend only stores the preference (`biometricEnabled`, read and written via `PATCH /account/settings`, section 6.7) — it validates no biometrics. After passing the local barrier, the app uses the existing session (renewed via `POST /auth/refresh` when needed, or `POST /auth/login` if it has fully expired).

### 6.2 Ingestion and entries
| Endpoint | Requirement | AI involved |
|---|---|---|
| `POST /media/ocr` — the image is not persisted; only the extracted text moves on | RF02 | Claude Haiku 4.5 (vision) |
| `POST /entries` — creates an entry; internally triggers the PII check and embedding generation; accepts `source` (`manual`/`audio`/`photo`/`chat`) and `chatMessageId` when the origin is the chat | RF01, RF02, RF10 | Claude Haiku 4.5 (PII) + Voyage AI (embedding) |
| `GET /entries` — filters by `source`/`dateFrom`/`dateTo`; tags appear only embedded in the response, read-only | RF07 | — |
| `GET /entries/:id` | RF07 | — |

**No entry editing or deletion, and no tag endpoint — intentional:** entries are immutable once created ("original content intact, never censored"); there is no `PATCH`/`DELETE /entries/:id`. Tags are populated only by test seed data — no endpoint creates, deletes or filters by tag or category (see RF06). This is consistent with section 2: dynamic categorization was simplified to manual tags that receive no functional implementation.

### 6.3 Chat and memory (RAG)
| Endpoint | Requirement | AI involved |
|---|---|---|
| `POST /chat/sessions` — blocked offline | RF04 | — |
| `GET /chat/sessions` — works offline (cache) | RF04, RF07 | — |
| `GET /chat/sessions/:id/messages` — works offline (cache) | RF04 | — |
| `POST /chat/sessions/:id/messages` — streaming (SSE); blocked offline | RF04 | Voyage AI (question embedding) + Claude Sonnet 5 (response) |
| `POST /chat/sessions/:id/messages/:userMessageId/retry` — regenerates the response without duplicating the user's question; it supports "partial message visible with a failure indication, and a way to try again" in RF04 | RF04 | Voyage AI (embedding, reused from cache) + Claude Sonnet 5 (response) |
| `POST /chat/sessions/:id/insight` | RF08 | Claude Haiku 4.5 |
| `POST /entries` — called from the "save to journal" button (see 6.2) | RF10 | Claude Haiku 4.5 (PII) + Voyage AI (embedding) |

### 6.4 Search
| Endpoint | Requirement | AI involved |
|---|---|---|
| `GET /entries/search?q=&source=&dateFrom=&dateTo=&limit=` — no `category` (see RF06) | RF06 | Voyage AI (query embedding) |

### 6.5 Export
| Endpoint | Requirement | AI involved |
|---|---|---|
| `POST /export/summary` — asynchronous job | RF05 | Claude Haiku 4.5 |
| `GET /export/:jobId/status` | RF05 | — |
| `GET /export/:jobId/download` | RF05 | — |

### 6.6 Dashboard
| Endpoint | Requirement | AI involved |
|---|---|---|
| `GET /dashboard/aggregate?period=` — separate from the text so it does not block the chart | RF09 | — |
| `GET /dashboard/narrative?period=` | RF09 | Claude Haiku 4.5 |

### 6.7 Account
| Endpoint | Requirement | AI involved |
|---|---|---|
| `PATCH /account/settings` — includes the persona toggle (extension) | RNF05, extension | — |
| `DELETE /account` | RNF05 | — |

| Error handling | `fpdart` (`Either<Failure, T>`) |

| Parameter | Value | Requirement |
|---|---|---|
| Background session timeout | 5 min | RF03 |
| Search debounce | 300 ms | RF06 |
| Proactive insight trigger | 5 messages OR 2 min of inactivity | RF08 |
| Dashboard rendering scenarios | 0 / 1 / > 30 entries | RF09 |
| Minimum test coverage (domain) | ≥ 80% | RNF07 |
| Local UI latency | < 100 ms | RNF01 |
| Loading-indicator threshold | > 300 ms | RNF01 |
| Network-error scenarios tested | 5 endpoints × 3 failures = 15 | RNF09 |

---

## 11. Error codes (RNF09)

Every endpoint returns `{ code, message, retryable }`. Minimum codes the app handles:

| Code | Situation | `retryable` |
|---|---|---|
| `AUTH_EXPIRED` | Session expired, re-authentication needed | no |
| `AUTH_INVALID` | Invalid credentials / biometrics | no |
| `NETWORK_TIMEOUT` | Request exceeded the time limit | yes |
| `NETWORK_OFFLINE` | No connection — action blocked (see RF04/RF06) | yes |
| `VALIDATION_ERROR` | Malformed request body | no |
| `PII_CHECK_FAILED` | PII check failed before persisting | yes |
| `EMBEDDING_FAILED` | Voyage AI unavailable / error | yes |
| `AI_GENERATION_TIMEOUT` | Claude did not respond in time (chat/insight/summary/dashboard) | yes |
| `NOT_FOUND` | Resource does not exist or does not belong to the user | no |
| `RATE_LIMITED` | Request limit exceeded | yes |

The complete, closed list of the backend's 13 codes, with HTTP statuses, is in `docs/input/backend/error-taxonomy.md`.

---

## 12. Delivery order

Work is delivered in units, one per functional requirement, preceded by a foundation unit, in this order:

**F000 → RF03 → RF01 → RF02 → RF07 → RF06 → RF04 → RF10 → RF08 → RF05 → RF09**

- **F000 (foundation)** covers what no single requirement owns but all of them use: project scaffold, `design_tokens.dart`, HTTP client returning `Either`, login and sign-up (Screen 0.1a in the prototype), base navigation and expired-session handling.
- RF10 comes after RF01 and RF04; RF08 comes after RF04.

---

## 13. Technical constraints

**Fixed:**
- Flutter and Dart at the version pinned for the repository (fvm).
- State management: `flutter_bloc`.
- Clean Architecture, three layers per feature.
- Error handling: `fpdart`; repositories return `Either<Failure, T>`.
- Test doubles: `mocktail`.
- On-device speech-to-text: `whisper_ggml`.
- Visual tokens: `lib/core/design_tokens.dart` is the single source of colors, typography, spacing and radii.
- Platform: iOS, portrait only.
- Folder convention:

```
lib/
  core/
  features/
    <feature>/
      data/
      domain/
      presentation/
```

**Free (choose what fits):** routing, HTTP client, local cache, dependency injection, secure storage, biometrics package, chart package.

usage: memlog.py [-h] {init,append,set} ...

memlog — an append-only memory log: LLM-optimal working memory for a skill.

A memlog is the dense, chronological record of everything that mattered in a piece of
work — every item the user generated or accepted — kept minimal like human memory: only
what's important, never bloated. It persists ACROSS sessions, so a fresh session can
load it and continue. It is NOT a deliverable; downstream artifacts (a brief, a PRD, a
deck, a report) are *derived* from it on demand. The host skill supplies the vocabulary
by how it calls `append` — the tool stays neutral.

It is a FLAT log: there are no sections or grouping. Every entry is one line, recorded
at the END in the order it happened. The chronology itself is the structure — an event
like "started technique X" is just another entry, same as an idea or an insight.

Three invariants make it trustworthy:

  1. Append-only, chronological. Entries land at the end, in the order they happen.
     Nothing is ever inserted backward, reordered, edited, or removed. There is no
     edit or delete subcommand by design; history is never rewritten.
  2. Write-only / blind. Every command is an atomic, context-free write and echoes the
     new state as one line of JSON, so the caller never re-reads the file mid-session.
     The one time the file is read is on resume — and the caller reads it itself, not
     via this script.
  3. No lifecycle status. A memory log has no "complete" flag. Whether the work is done,
     blocked, or paused is itself a fact that happened, so it is recorded as an entry
     (e.g. `append --type event --text "session complete"`), never as frontmatter the
     log would have to mutate. The chronology stays the single source of truth, and a
     resume learns the state by reading the last entries — the same way it learns
     everything else.

Atomicity: every write goes to a temp file, is flushed and fsync'd, then atomically
renamed over the target, so a crash never leaves a half-written entry.

The file shape (.memlog.md):

    ---
    topic: Onboarding flow for a budgeting app
    goal: lift week-1 retention
    updated: 2026-06-07T14:22
    ---

    - (note) user picked techniques: SCAMPER, then Six Thinking Hats
    - (technique) started SCAMPER
    - (idea) skip the signup wall: let people try with sample data first
    - (idea) auto-import one bank account so the first screen shows real numbers
    - (question) is open-banking consent too heavy for step one?
    - (insight) the "scary numbers" risk and the "real numbers" idea are one lever: show real data, pre-categorized
    - (direction) optimize for the anxious first-timer, not the power user
    - (decision) lead with one pre-categorized account; defer multi-account import

# Product Brief: Cerne

## Executive Summary

Cerne is a reflective-journaling mobile app whose AI assistant actually remembers the user — it answers from a RAG search over the user's own past entries, instead of the stateless, generic-sounding responses that dominate the AI-journaling category today. The user captures their day by text, voice, or photo; the assistant surfaces connections across that personal record in conversation, offers occasional unprompted insight, and lets the user fold a chat realization straight into their journal with one tap.

[ASSUMPTION] This brief is being produced as a TCC (undergraduate capstone) deliverable: a bridge document that consolidates the problem/solution/scope already explored in the project's PRFAQ and F000 foundation-decision sessions into the shape the next BMad stage (PRD → architecture → build) expects, and that can also stand as the "what and why" section of the written defense. It is evaluated on engineering discipline under a frozen backend contract and a fixed delivery order, not on commercial traction — there are no unit economics or acquisition targets here, and none should be invented for this document.

The differentiator is narrow and deliberate: not a bigger feature set, but a better memory. Competitive research (see addendum) confirms "generic AI response" fatigue is the single most common complaint against AI-journaling incumbents (Mindsera, Rosebud, Reflectly, Day One AI) — Cerne is positioned directly against that gap, backed by an explicitly non-clinical stance that is a timing advantage rather than just a legal fence, given the current regulatory pressure on companion-chatbot framing.

## The Problem

**[ASSUMPTION — reconstructed, not stated in `docs/input/`]** `docs/input/requirements.md` specifies screens and endpoints, never a customer. The persona and problem below are inferred from UI language (Portuguese), architectural choices (on-device STT, zero AI-pipeline retention, explicit non-clinical scope), and the extension features that were deliberately cut — they should be treated as a working hypothesis for the brief and defense, not a sourced fact.

Someone who journals, or has tried to and quit — paper, Notes, Day One — or who already talks to a general-purpose chatbot (ChatGPT) to process their day. The chatbot forgets everything between sessions, so every conversation restarts from zero; the journal, when kept, is a one-way write into a void that never responds. Both leave the same need unmet: being understood *in light of one's own history*, not generically. A secondary, quieter fear sits underneath — that a private, emotionally loaded diary is being mined, sold, or silently reinterpreted as a mental-health signal.

## The Solution

Capture is multimodal and deliberately unceremonious — text, a voice note transcribed on-device, or a photo OCR'd server-side — and every capture becomes a durable entry, never a disposable chat turn. Chat is the daily surface: a continuous conversation where the assistant's answers are grounded in semantic search over the user's own entries (RAG), not canned reflection prompts. The two pipelines are deliberately decoupled — a chat message writes to the journal only when the user explicitly says so ("save to journal," RF10) — so the assistant can be talked to freely without every utterance becoming a permanent record.

## What Makes This Different

Base directory for this skill: /Users/wagnerduarte/Documents/Faculdade/2026.2/TCC/cerne-ciclo-b/.claude/skills/bmad-help

# BMad Help

## Purpose

Help the user understand where they are in their BMad workflow and what to do next, and also answer broader questions when asked that could be augmented with remote sources such as module documentation sources.

## Desired Outcomes

When this skill completes, the user should:

1. **Know where they are** — which module and phase they're in, what's already been completed
2. **Know what to do next** — the next recommended and/or required step, with clear reasoning
3. **Know how to invoke it** — skill name, menu code, action context, and any args that shortcut the conversation
4. **Get offered a quick start** — when a single skill is the clear next step, offer to run it for the user right now rather than just listing it
5. **Feel oriented, not overwhelmed** — surface only what's relevant to their current position; don't dump the entire catalog
6. **Get answers to general questions** — when the question doesn't map to a specific skill, use the module's registered documentation to give a grounded answer

## Data Sources

- **Catalog**: `{project-root}/_bmad/_config/bmad-help.csv` — assembled manifest of all installed module skills
- **Config**: Run `uv run {project-root}/_bmad/scripts/resolve_config.py --project-root {project-root}` and use the merged JSON to resolve `output-location` variables and read `core.communication_language` and `modules.bmm.project_knowledge`. The resolver merges `_bmad/config.toml`, `_bmad/config.user.toml`, `_bmad/custom/config.toml`, and `_bmad/custom/config.user.toml` in that order.
- **Artifacts**: Files matching `outputs` patterns at resolved `output-location` paths reveal which steps are possibly completed; their content may also provide grounding context for recommendations
- **Project knowledge**: If `project_knowledge` resolves to an existing path, read it for grounding context. Never fabricate project-specific details.
- **Module docs**: Rows with `_meta` in the `skill` column carry a URL or path in `output-location` pointing to the module's documentation (e.g., llms.txt). Fetch and use these to answer general questions about that module.

## CSV Interpretation

The catalog uses this format:

```
module,skill,display-name,menu-code,description,action,args,phase,preceded-by,followed-by,required,output-location,outputs
```

**Phases** determine the high-level flow:
- `anytime` — available regardless of workflow state
- Skills group into folders (`plan`, `ship`; some modules use numbered phases) and flow in order; naming varies by module

**Sequencing** determines recommended ordering within and across phases (these are soft suggestions, not hard gates — see `required` for gating):
- `preceded-by` — skills that should ideally complete before this one
- `followed-by` — skills that should ideally run after this one
- Format: `skill-name` for single-action skills, `skill-name:action` for multi-action skills

**Required gates**:
- `required=true` items must complete before the user can meaningfully proceed to later phases
- A phase with no required items is entirely optional — recommend it but be clear about what's actually required next

**Completion detection**:
- Search resolved output paths for `outputs` patterns
- Fuzzy-match found files to catalog rows
- User may also state completion explicitly, or it may be evident from the current conversation

**Descriptions carry routing context** — some contain cycle info and alternate paths (e.g., "back to DS if fixes needed"). Read them as navigation hints, not just display text.

## Response Format

For each recommended item, present:
- `[menu-code]` **Display name** — e.g., "[PR] PRD"
- Skill name in backticks — e.g., `bmad-prd`
- For multi-action skills: action invocation context — e.g., "dev lets run a code review!"
- Description if present in CSV; otherwise your existing knowledge of the skill suffices
- Args if available

**Ordering**: Show optional items first, then the next required item. Make it clear which is which.

## Constraints

- Present all output in `{communication_language}`
- Recommend running each skill in a **fresh context window**
- Match the user's tone — conversational when they're casual, structured when they want specifics
- If the active module is ambiguous, retrieve all meta rows remote sources to find relevant info also to help answer their question
